title: Why IndiGo loses ₹680 per flyer despite 34% yield jump

outro.text: Will fares hold if fuel eases? The December 1 price decides. Yield up 34 percent yet each flyer loses 680 rupees.

sources: IndiGo Q2 FY27 press release (BSE filing, Oct. 29, 2026)

scenes.text: Yield up 34 percent yet each flyer loses 680 rupees.
Fuel per passenger jumped 75 percent to 3,624 rupees.
But the real twist: six of ten lost rupees came from currency, not flying.
A thousand-dollar bill now costs 8,000 rupees more than a year ago.
Cost per passenger 9,520 rupees, loss per passenger 680 rupees.
Next clue: December 1, when jet fuel is repriced.

funnel.long_title: Your IndiGo ticket costs more. So why is IndiGo still losing money?
